sourceNote: Transcribed from the supplied Law Mock PDF editions: prelims-2019.pdf, prelims-2020.pdf, prelims-2022.pdf and prelims-2023.pdf. Source numbering and duplicated questions are retained. Includes 314 keyed questions and the unkeyed 2020 Q67 fragment. For needs-review records, note gives the printed answer letter where available, and correctAnswer is null so the practice engine does not score the item. Explanations reflect the supplied solutions, including errors and guesses discussed in the notes. Statutory references are for the historical papers.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Additional Evidence means :
options: evidence let in appeal before the trial has closed in the lower Court, it is a privilege allowed only under special circumstances
evidence let in appeal after the trial has closed in the Supreme Court, it is a privilege allowed only under special circumstances
evidence let in appeal after the trial has closed in the lower Court, it is a privilege allowed only under special circumstances
questions.explanation: Additional evidence is evidence let in on appeal after the trial has closed in the lower court; a privilege allowed only under special circumstances (Order 41 Rule 27 CPC / Section 391 CrPC).
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order XLI Rule 27; Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 391

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following deals with the absence of a complainant ?
options: Section 235 of the Criminal Procedure Code
Section 264 of the Criminal Procedure Code
Section 249 of the Criminal Procedure Code
Section 242 of the Criminal Procedure Code
questions.explanation: Section 249 CrPC empowers the Magistrate to discharge the accused on the absence of the complainant (before charge, where offence is compoundable or non-cognizable).

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: A sues B for land of which B is in possession, and which, as A asserts, was left to A by the will of C, B's father. If no evidence were given on either side, B would be entitled to retain his possession. Applying Section 102 of the Indian Evidence Act :
options: the burden of proof is on A
the burden of proof is on B
the burden of proof is on C
questions.explanation: Under Section 102 of the Evidence Act burden lies on the party who would fail if no evidence were given; since B (in possession) would retain the land, the burden of proof is on A.

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: When the power has obtained possession of the goods pledged by him under a contract voidable is not rescinded at the time of pledge, the pawnee acquires_____.
questions.explanation: Under Section 178A of the Contract Act, where the pawnor obtained possession under a voidable contract not rescinded at the time of pledge, the pawnee (acting in good faith) acquires a good title to the goods.
questions.note: The stem is incomplete or materially garbled. PDF answer key: A.

options: A has committed an offence under section 322 of the Indian Penal code
A has committed an offence under section 328 of the Indian Penal Code
A has committed an offence under section 330 of the Indian Penal Code
A has committed an offence under section 334 of the Indian Penal code

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: Making the atmosphere noxious to health is dealt with.
questions.explanation: Making the atmosphere noxious to health is dealt with under Section 278 IPC.

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: "Tort" in the limitation Act, 1963 includes which of the following?
options: Civil wrong, which is exclusively the breach of a contract or the breach of trust
Judicial wrong, which is not exclusively the breach of a contract or the breast of trust
Civil wrong, which is not exclusively the breach of a contract or the breach of trust
questions.explanation: Section 2(m) of the Limitation Act, 1963 defines 'tort' as a civil wrong which is not exclusively the breach of a contract or the breach of a trust.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following is true of the right to receive maintenance under section 125 of the criminal Procedure code?
options: It is purely a personal right created by an order of criminal court
There is no charge created on property by the order for maintenance
The maintenance cannot be held to the alienable property
questions.explanation: The right to maintenance under Section 125 CrPC is a personal right created by the criminal court's order, creates no charge on property, and the maintenance cannot be made alienable - hence all of these are true.

questions.subject: Computer Awareness
questions.question: Where a row and a column meet, is called____.
questions.explanation: The intersection of a row and a column in a spreadsheet is called a cell.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: By which amendment act to the constitution of India, the provision with regard to compulsory acquisition of property was omitted?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 omitted Article 31 (which dealt with compulsory acquisition of property) and deleted the right to property as a fundamental right, replacing it with Article 300A.

Before a person whom the accused already knows

options: Payment of interest on the money due from the defendant to the plaintiff
Payment of interest on the money due from the plaintiff to the defendant
questions.explanation: Article 25 of the Limitation Act, 1963 prescribes the period for money payable for interest upon money due from the defendant to the plaintiff (3 years from when interest becomes due).

questions.question: False statement, rumour, etc. circulated with intent to cause mutiny or offence against the public peace is dealt under

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: X has been illegally detained by the police authorities. His father has been advised to file a writ petition before the High Court. Which writ should be prayed for in such petitions?
questions.explanation: For illegal detention by the police, the appropriate writ is Habeas Corpus, which commands production of the detained person before the court.
questions.reference: Constitution of India, Articles 226 and 32 (habeas corpus)

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following provisions of the code of civil procedure will be applicable in case of death of one of the several defendants or the sole defendant in the suit?
questions.explanation: Order 22 Rule 4 CPC governs the death of one of several defendants or the sole defendant, providing for substitution of the legal representative.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order 22 Rule 4

questions.subject: Limitation
questions.question: Under Section 6(2), limitation act, 1963 where several disabilities co-exist concurrently or where the plaintiff is affected by another disability from earlier disability,______.
options: Time will commence even if both the disabilities have not cased
Time will not commence till both the disabilities have crashed
Time will not commence till any one of the disabilities has cased
questions.explanation: Under Section 6(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963, where several disabilities co-exist or a further disability supervenes, time will not commence till both (all) the disabilities have ceased.
questions.note: The keyed option says 'crashed' where the solution says 'ceased'. PDF answer key: B.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following states when accused shall be discharged?
options: Section 239 of code of Criminal Procedure
Section 264 of Code of Criminal Procedure
Section 337 of Code of Criminal Procedure
Section 258 of Code of Criminal Procedure
questions.explanation: Section 239 CrPC provides that in a warrant case instituted on a police report, if upon consideration the Magistrate finds the charge groundless, he shall discharge the accused.

questions.explanation: The tangible (physical) components of a computer system are collectively called hardware; software is intangible.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Under which of the following provisions of the code of civil procedure, the particulars of set-off are to be given in the written statements?
questions.explanation: Order 8 Rule 6 CPC requires the defendant to give particulars of a set-off in the written statement, which then has the effect of a plaint in a cross-suit.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following deals with power to amend decree or order where appeal is summarily dismissed in the Code of Civil Procedure ?
questions.explanation: Section 153A CPC gives the court of first instance power to amend the decree/order under Section 152 where the appeal has been summarily dismissed under Order 41 Rule 11.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: A suit for partition contains which of the following decree ?
questions.explanation: A partition suit ordinarily proceeds in two stages, producing both a preliminary decree (declaring shares) and a final decree (effecting actual division by metes and bounds).
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order XX Rule 18
questions.note: Option D contains an OCR symbol in place of an option label. PDF answer key: D.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Under which of the following provisions of the code of civil procedure, the prismer is required to be brought to court in custody?
questions.explanation: Order 16A Rule 6 CPC requires the officer in charge of the prison to cause the named prisoner to be brought to and kept in custody in or near the court.
questions.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order 16A Rule 6

questions.question: Which section of the Gujarat Prohibition Act provides for procedure in confiscation ?

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: Which of the following is essential of an offence under Section 114, of Indian Penal Code '
options: the act was actually committed in pursuance of abetment
the accused was present while the act was being committed
questions.explanation: Section 114 IPC (abettor present when offence committed) requires abetment by the accused, that the act was committed in pursuance of the abetment, and the accused's presence at the time of commission - all of these.

questions.subject: Negotiable Instruments
questions.question: What is the presumption to be drawn under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act ?
options: That the holder of the cheque received the cheque for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
That the drawer had duly signed the cheque.
That the cheque was dishonoured for want of sufficient funds;
That the cheque in question had not expired on the date of its presentation
questions.explanation: Section 139 NI Act raises the presumption that the holder of the cheque received it for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, unless the contrary is proved.

questions.subject: Evidence
questions.question: The principle___is embodied in section 6 of the evidence acts.
options: Falsus in uno falsus in omentum
questions.explanation: Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act embodies the doctrine of res gestae - facts forming part of the same transaction are relevant.

questions.subject: Computer Awareness

questions.subject: Evidence

questions.explanation: Under subsequent conduct (relevant under Section 8 of the Evidence Act), change of life, evasion of justice, and fear/trembling are all material - all of these.

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: Which of the following deals with alternative promise, one branch being illegal in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 ?

A question asked with reasonable ground

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question: Where a promissory note is payable by instalments have become due, and the holder of the note sues only for one of the instalments and consists of sure for the other instalments.
options: He can afterwards sue for these instalments
He cannot afterwards sue for these instalments

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Which of the following deals with the period of detention undergone by the accused to be set off against the sentence of imprisonment?
questions.explanation: Section 428 CrPC provides that the period of detention undergone by the accused during investigation, inquiry or trial shall be set off against the term of imprisonment imposed on conviction.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: To prove both the parts of the offence contemplated in section 116 of the Indian Penal code, which of the following must be proved by the prosecution?
options: To prove the first part, the accused did abet the offence either by instigation or by conspiracy or by international aiding or by illegal commission
to prove the first part, the offence was such which is punishable with imprisonment.
to prove the second part, the person abetted was a public servant during the period he was abetted.
to prove the second part, it was the duty of such public servants to prevent the commission of such an offence.
questions.explanation: Under Section 116 IPC (abetment of an offence punishable with imprisonment, where the offence is not committed), the first part requires proof that the accused abetted the offence by instigation, conspiracy or intentional aiding; option (a) correctly states this limb.
questions.note: The keyed option contains corrupted wording about the modes of abetment. PDF answer key: A.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following latitudes pass through India ?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 N) passes through India, traversing eight states; the Equator, Arctic Circle and Tropic of Capricorn do not.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question: Find the odd one out

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: A sees Z commit what appears to A to be a murder. A, in the exercise to the best of his judgement exerted in good faith, of the power which the law gives to all persons of apprehending murderers in the act, seizes Z, in order to bring Z before the proper authorities.
options: A has committed an offence, while Z was acting in self-defence
Both A and Z committed an offence
A has committed no offence, though it may turn out that Z was acting in self-defence
questions.explanation: This is the illustration to the general exception (good faith, mistake of fact, Section 79 IPC): A, apprehending what appears to be a murderer in good faith exercise of the power law gives all persons, commits no offence even if Z turns out to have acted in self-defence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Expedient (Choose the Synonym)

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: How does Section 157 of Criminal Procedure code provides safeguards for rape victims ?
options: The recording of statement of the victim shall be conducted at the residence of the victim or in the place of her choice
The recording of statement as far as practicable must be conducted by a woman police officer in the presence of her parent or guardian or near relatives or social worker of the locality
questions.explanation: The proviso to Section 157 CrPC requires, for rape offences, that the victim's statement be recorded at her residence or place of her choice and, as far as practicable, by a woman police officer in the presence of her parent/guardian/near relative/social worker; both (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: Which of the following deals with how delivery to bailee is to be made in the indian contract act, 1872.
questions.explanation: Section 149 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 deals with how delivery to a bailee is made: by doing anything which has the effect of putting the goods in the possession of the bailee or of any person authorised to hold them on his behalf.

questions.subject: Criminal Procedure
questions.question: Autrefois acquit or plea of double jeopardy arises:
options: When a person is acquitted again of the same offence
When a person is convicted again for the different offence
When a person is tried again for the same offence
questions.explanation: Autrefois acquit (and the double jeopardy bar under Section 300 CrPC / Article 20(2)) arises when a person is tried again for the same offence after a prior acquittal or conviction.
questions.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 300; Constitution of India, Article 20(2)

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I needed to study, but I kept beating around the bush. (Give the appropriate meaning to the underlined portion)
questions.explanation: 'Beating around the bush' is an idiom meaning to avoid the main topic and not come straight to the point.

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: Which of the following is false of Section 34 and Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code ?
options: Section 34 does not by itself create any specific offence whereas Section 149 does so.
Some active participation in crime is required in Section 34 while it is not needed in Section 149
Section 34 speaks of common intention while Section 149 contemplates common object
Section 34 requires at least five persons who must share the common intention while Section 149 requires at least two persons to share the common intention
questions.explanation: Statement (d) is false: Section 149 IPC (unlawful assembly) requires at least five persons sharing a common object, whereas Section 34 requires at least two persons sharing a common intention; option (d) reverses these requirements.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 51A of the Constitution of India provides for :
options: promotion of international peace and security
organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
questions.explanation: Article 51A of the Constitution of India (inserted by the 42nd Amendment) enumerates the Fundamental Duties of citizens.

questions.subject: Contract Law
questions.question: A agrees to sell to B the goods which are on their way to Chennai from Oman by a ship. But before the agreement between the parties, the ship had sunk and the goods to be sold to B, were lost. Neither party is aware of this happening. The agreement is :
questions.explanation: Under Section 20 of the Contract Act (mistake of fact as to a matter essential to the agreement) and Section 6 of the Sale of Goods Act (goods perishing before the contract without the knowledge of either party), the agreement is void.
questions.reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 20; Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 6

questions.subject: Indian Penal Code
questions.question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property or a valuable security or to constrain to do anything, which is, illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence is dealt under
questions.explanation: Section 329 IPC punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property/valuable security or to constrain a person to do anything illegal or which may facilitate an offence.

questions.question: When a file is saved for the first time____________.
options: it must be given a name to identify it
it does not need a name
it only needs a name if it is not going to be printed
